solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Plug souse with pork as ingredient

indicators.note: an ingredient goes into a mixture, so the pork word is put inside the souse word

parts.note: a souse is a drunkard, a sot
pork is the meat of the pig

explanation.surface: A recipe note: pickle the pork in brine, but it reads as a food instruction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Souse' looks like a verb for pickling; here it is a noun meaning a drunkard.
explanation.definitionFit: A spigot is a peg or stopper for the vent of a cask, a kind of plug.

clue.text: Head of falcon with droopier wing forward

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, taken here from falcon

parts.note: lank hair hangs limp, so lanker means droopier

explanation.surface: A falcon's head with a sagging wing pushed forward: a bird in poor shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wing forward' looks like bird anatomy but is a rugby position.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby union a flanker is the modern name for a wing forward in the back row of the scrum.

clue.text: Dependent worker with an eternity left in movement

indicators.note: the eternity and left pieces are placed in the movement word

parts.note: a wave is a movement, as of the hand or of water
ages is a colloquial term for a very long time

explanation.surface: A downtrodden labourer stuck forever in a political movement.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone wholly reliant on a wage for survival, with no other means, is a dependent worker in the pejorative idiom.

clue.text: Constant number generally divided by zero is divided in two

indicators.note: the zero word separates the two letters, sitting between them

parts.note: C is the usual symbol for a constant
N stands for a number in general, as in 'to the nth'
love is zero in tennis scoring

explanation.surface: A mathematical statement about dividing a constant by zero, which is undefined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divided by zero' looks like arithmetic; it means the tennis score stands between C and N.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloven hoof is split into two parts, so the word means split or cleft.

clue.text: Thrash Ulster in the middle of offensive

indicators.note: the Ulster letters are set in the middle of the offensive word

parts.note: a push is a military offensive
NI is Northern Ireland, often called Ulster

explanation.surface: Reports of a beating amid a military offensive in Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: To thrash someone is to beat them as a penalty, a synonym for chastise.

clue.text: Transfix or slay, roughly piercing skin

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go into the skin word, piercing it

parts.note: to pare fruit is to skin it

indicators.note: roughly signals that the letters of slay are worked loosely into a new order

explanation.surface: A choice between immobilising or killing, done roughly by stabbing through the skin.
explanation.walkthrough: The word 'or' is a link, not part of the fodder, and 'skin' is a verb, as in peeling fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: To transfix is to make someone motionless with shock or awe, the same as rendering them immobile.

clue.text: Encourage good among 27

indicators.note: the good letter is placed among the letters of the 27 synonym

parts.note: the answer to 27 down means unclothed, a synonym of nude

explanation.surface: A cheer of encouragement for a good person in a crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 27 refers to 27 down, which means without clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A gentle push to get someone to act is a form of encouragement or prompting.

clue.text: Airport stoppage detains holy woman

indicators.note: the stoppage word holds the holy woman inside it

parts.note: a stand is a halt or stoppage, as in come to a stand
Ste is the abbreviation for sainte, a female saint

explanation.surface: A security halt at an airport where a nun is held for questioning.
explanation.walkthrough: STE is the French feminine form of the saint abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Stansted is one of London's main airports, in Essex.

clue.text: Plain china, whitish with black inset

parts.note: china is rhyming slang (china plate, mate) for pal

indicators.note: the black letter is set inside the whitish word

parts.note: pale means whitish in colour
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A description of plain off-white porcelain with a black inlay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plain' and 'china' look like a crockery description; china is rhyming slang for mate.
explanation.definitionFit: Something plain is obvious or evident, and so readily perceived or felt.

clue.text: Greek's cross, interrupted by vulgar Canadian leader

indicators.note: the vulgar word breaks into the cross word

parts.note: tau is the Greek letter T, the shape of a T-cross
rude means vulgar or coarse

explanation.surface: An angry Greek interrupted by a crude Canadian politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek's cross' suggests an annoyed Greek; it is the T-shaped letter tau.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierre and Justin Trudeau both served as Prime Minister of Canada.

clue.text: Device for spraying glue, extremely sticky stuff

parts.note: a spray gun is a device for spraying paint

indicators.note: extremely points to the extreme letters, the first and last, of glue

explanation.surface: A glue gun spraying something extremely sticky.
explanation.definitionFit: A slang word for any unpleasant sticky or slimy substance.

clue.text: Flowering plant and swedes lie abandoned

indicators.note: abandoned means wild or uninhibited, so the letters are rearranged freely

explanation.surface: Turnips and other swedes left lying in an abandoned field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' looks like left behind; here it means unrestrained, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An Alpine plant with white woolly flowers, an example of a flowering plant.

clue.text: United upset by this cause of slippery grass

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the word reads from the bottom up

parts.note: wed means united in marriage

explanation.surface: A football team beaten on a slippery pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'United' looks like a football club; it means married.
explanation.definitionFit: Morning moisture condensing on the lawn makes the grass wet and slippery.

clue.text: Woods can't develop past this point involving staggering sensation

indicators.note: the point word wraps around the staggering word

parts.note: a tine is a point, a prong of a fork or of an antler
a reel is a dizzy, staggering feeling

explanation.surface: A forest unable to grow beyond a certain dizzying height.
explanation.walkthrough: 'point' belongs to the wordplay, not the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: On a mountain, the altitude above which forest cannot grow marks the limit of woodland.

clue.text: Cutter in Welsh river runs beyond Snowdonia's borders

indicators.note: the river and runs come beyond, after, the border letters
the borders of a word are its outer letters, here of Snowdonia

parts.note: the Wye rises in Wales
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A woodcutter working along a Welsh river near Snowdonia.
explanation.definitionFit: A person whose job is sawing timber is a cutter of wood.

clue.text: Bank job possibly held by a jerk denying being who's in charge?

indicators.note: the robbery word is held inside the jerk word, after the A

parts.note: a tic is an involuntary jerk
a heist is a robbery, and a bank job is one example

explanation.surface: A twitching robber caught during a bank raid, denying he is the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'being who's in charge' is God, so the definition means denying God exists.
explanation.definitionFit: An unbeliever denies the existence of a supreme being in charge of the universe.

clue.text: Protective shell of automobile at speed

parts.note: a car is an automobile
apace means quickly, at speed

explanation.surface: The protective shell of a car racing at high speed.
explanation.definitionFit: The hard upper shell of a tortoise or crab protects the animal.

clue.text: Some have gravy as accompaniment for meat

indicators.note: some of the phrase means a part of it, so the letters are picked from inside have gravy

explanation.surface: Diners pouring gravy over their meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Vegetables, informally shortened, are the usual side dish served with meat.

clue.text: Wrapped in pastry and cooked once? True

indicators.note: cooked means altered or falsified, as in cooked books, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cook confirming a dish was once baked in pastry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' looks like part of the kitchen scene but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A French culinary term for food baked inside a pastry crust.

clue.text: Black fly

definitions.meaning: a hard black stone, also used of a deep black colour

explanation.surface: A dark insect.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a glossy black mineral and travel by jet plane.

clue.text: Slightly wet obstruction in river enclosure

parts.note: a dam is a barrier across a river
a pen is an enclosure for animals

explanation.surface: A slightly damp barrier in a river beside a sheep pen.
explanation.definitionFit: To moisten a little is a synonym for making slightly wet.

clue.text: Ace and 6 short

indicators.note: short means cut off at the end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: 6 refers to 6 down, whose meaning, encourage with a poke, has the synonym prod

explanation.surface: A playing card and the number six.
explanation.walkthrough: 6 is 6 down.
explanation.definitionFit: An ace is an expert or professional, a top performer.

clue.text: Compile stirring diatribe

indicators.note: stirring mixes things up, so the letters of compile are rearranged

explanation.surface: Instructions to put together a rousing rant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stirring' looks like an adjective for the diatribe but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A fierce verbal or written attack on someone is a diatribe.

clue.text: Hungry sense after wild party

indicators.note: the sense word comes after the party word

parts.note: a rave is a wild party
nous is common sense

explanation.surface: Starving and only coming to your senses after an all-night party.
explanation.definitionFit: Being extremely hungry is the core meaning of the word, starving.

clue.text: No cooler in crowds?

definitions.meaning: split into two words, the phrase means equally hot, not cooler

explanation.surface: A packed crowd that is no cooler.
explanation.walkthrough: Split (2,4) the answer gives the 'no cooler' sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Teeming with people or insects in a dense throng means being in crowds.

clue.text: Attempt to restrict gag that's rambling, long and coarse

indicators.note: the attempt word encloses the jumbled letters

parts.note: a shy is a throw or attempt, as at a coconut shy

indicators.note: rambling means wandering, so the letters of gag are rearranged

explanation.surface: A comedian trying to curb a long-winded joke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Attempt' is a noun, as in having a shy at a coconut, and the definition is the last three words together.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair or fur that is long, rough and unkempt is described with this word.

clue.text: Drinking establishment backing turf was racing charity

parts.note: a bar is a drinking establishment

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the turf and racing words read in reverse

parts.note: sod is a piece of turf
ran means was racing

explanation.surface: A pub backing a horse on the turf to raise money for charity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns SOD RAN into NARDOS.
explanation.definitionFit: Barnardo's is a long-standing British children's charity.

clue.text: Writhed with no top on, nor anything else

indicators.note: with no top on, the first letter is removed from the word

parts.note: to snake is to move sinuously, to writhe

explanation.surface: Someone writhing about wearing no top and nothing else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no top on, nor anything else' reads as one description; the definition is the final words.
explanation.definitionFit: Wearing nothing at all, neither a top nor anything else, is the state of being unclothed.

clue.text: This? Dramatic piece in opera, ultimately

definitions.text: This? Dramatic piece in opera, ultimately

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so the final letter of each of the first five words is taken

explanation.surface: A question asking whether this is a dramatic piece in an opera.
explanation.definitionFit: A scena is a dramatic solo scene in an opera, a piece for a single singer.

clue.text: In France, you sanction legislation reversing industrial action

indicators.note: the three pieces in clue order are read backwards

parts.note: tu is the French for you
to OK something is to sanction it
law is legislation

explanation.surface: French workers approving a law that reverses strike action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversing' turns TUOKLAW back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: A strike in which workers leave their workplace is a form of industrial protest.

clue.text: Going round circuit with acid

parts.note: OR is a logic gate, a circuit in electronics
an acid remark is biting, sharp

explanation.surface: A race lap taken with corrosive chemicals.
explanation.walkthrough: An OR gate is a digital logic circuit.
explanation.definitionFit: Circling a planet or star is travelling round it in a path.

clue.text: Butt in when hearing gong

indicators.note: when hearing means the word is taken as spoken, by its sound

parts.note: gong is slang for a medal

explanation.surface: Interrupting when a gong sounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gong' looks like a percussion instrument; it is British slang for a medal.
explanation.definitionFit: To interfere in others' affairs uninvited is to intrude or interfere.
